unit.title: Combinational Logic as a Tested Interface
unit.scope: Specify, implement, and exhaustively test a one-bit full adder and a four-bit ripple-carry adder as a deterministic Python model.
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student with introductory programming experience who is beginning digital design and production-style engineering practice.
prerequisites: Comfort with functions, integer arithmetic, and binary representation
Ability to run Python 3 standard-library unittest tests
No Verilog, FPGA board, Vivado, textbook, or official assignment access required
learning_objectives: Translate a finite behavioral contract into bit-level Boolean logic
Compose a fixed-width component from a smaller verified component
Separate a production implementation from an independent test oracle
Use exhaustive finite-domain tests, explicit input validation, and reproducible evidence
Explain the correctness and dependency cost of ripple-carry composition

required_evidence: All required learner artifacts are present
Captured test evidence is reproducible and consistent with an examiner rerun
Independent examiner checks cover every valid input and the specified invalid-input behavior
The examiner-only rubric is applied without relying on the learner's prose claim
